steps: Run: Godot --headless --path . -s res://qa/bots/bot_run.gd -- --strategy=decent --seed=2 --market=mil --skip-tutorial (seeds 3 and 4 identical in result; seed 1 works)
Cycle 11-14: the bot buys chips and energy routes; at cycle 14 feed_log shows 'route to station' for energy and chips from planet 5 (ok true).
Cycle 27 (end): RESULT workshop_state munitions 'stalled', workshop_reason 'needs energy'. storage_end has no energy in any key; planet:5 holds 80 chips; craft_totals is empty.
Same command with --local-orders: storage empty, reason 'needs energy,chips'. Same command with --skip-skill=MIL_3: chips reach system:1 (244) but energy still 0.
expected: Once the feed routes are open, energy and chips reach system storage and munitions crafts cells (seed 1 of this batch crafted 81 cells).
actual: In seeds 2-4 no energy ever reaches any storage key, and chips stay in planet storage (seed 2) or reach it only without MIL_3 (seed 2 ablation). Munitions stays stalled for the whole run, so MIL_2, MIL_4 and MIL_6 cannot be measured in 3 of 4 seeds. Root cause UNKNOWN: either the energy buy source the bot picks (planet 5) or the route's delivery in route_engine.

steps: Run: Godot --headless --path . -s res://qa/bots/bot_run.gd -- --strategy=decent --seed=1 --market=mil --skip-tutorial. MIL_2, MIL_4 and MIL_6 learned by tech by cycle 19 (tech_log).
End state: craft_totals has cells 81 and no armour, although MIL_4 (armour unlock) is learned.
Run: --market=lux --seed=1 --skip-tutorial. LUX_4 (gems unlock) learned by tech at cycle 23. craft_totals has cask only, no gems.
expected: A tech that unlocks a good lets the bot craft it, or the design says the good is not meant to be fed at this stage.
actual: Armour needs energy, chips and rivets (3 raw inputs) and gems need ore, silk and musk (4 ship feeds). The bot's workshop feed limit (FEED_SHIPS = 2 in bot_run.gd) never allows either, so MIL_4 and LUX_4 never pay off in any run. Whether armour and gems are meant to be bot-feedable is UNKNOWN to QA.

steps: Run decent with --market=mil --skip-tutorial, seeds 1-4, and the default decent (no focus), seeds 1-4.
Mil focus: 4 of 4 wins at cycle 27, mil share 0.60-0.70. Default decent: 3 of 4 wins at cycle 27 (seed 3 SOFT at c40).
In 3 of 4 mil-focus seeds munitions is stalled (see BUG-1), so the win comes from mil goods lanes alone.
expected: No focus wins more reliably at the target pace unless the chain it is named for is what makes it win.
actual: Mil focus is the most reliable focus and wins at 27 without its workshop chain. Candidate for dominance; it may disappear once BUG-1 is fixed. Not a loss rule failure.

steps: Run: Godot --headless --path . -s res://qa/bots/bot_run.gd -- --strategy=decent --seed=1 --market=bio --skip-tutorial (seeds 2 and 3 likewise).
RESULT: outcome win at cycle 34 (seed 1), 32 (seed 2), 34 (seed 3); seed 4 win at 27. Culture lab running, bio share 0.59.
expected: A decent player wins between about cycle 22 and 30 (targets: skilled 22-26, no skills 26-30).
actual: Three of four bio-focus wins fall after cycle 30. The bio-focus runs are slow and cash-poor (mean final cash 7.1k vs 17-33k for the other focuses).

steps: Run: Godot --headless --path . -s res://qa/bots/bot_run.gd -- --strategy=decent --seed=3 --market=lux --skip-tutorial
RESULT: win at cycle 35; bio share 0.53, lux share 0.24. Seed 2 wins at 30; seeds 1 and 4 SOFT at c40.
expected: Decent player wins between about cycle 22 and 30.
actual: Win at cycle 35, after the pacing band. Lux focus wins in only 2 of 4 seeds (see the design note below).

steps: Run focus_lux (seeds 1-4) and abl_LUX_1 (same seeds, --skip-skill=LUX_1).
focus_lux wins: bio share 0.53-0.59 at the win, lux share 0.17-0.24. The win comes from the food route the atelier needs (cask = 3 food).
abl_LUX_1 (no atelier, no food route): 0 of 4 wins; lux share rises to 0.36 but the run ends SOFT at c40 in every seed.
expected: A lux focus win comes from the lux market share the lux tree builds.
actual: The lux focus wins through the bio market share. LUX_1 is the gate for that route, so the lux tree's own goods add little to the win. Economy intent is UNKNOWN to QA; this is a design check.

steps: Run: TAG=smoke_lux STRATEGIES=decent SEEDS=1 EXTRA='--market=lux --skip-tutorial' bash qa/bots/run_batch.sh <out> with TMPDIR at the default macOS value (/var/folders/.../T/). Log size 1 line.
Godot exited after its version line with no RESULT and no error; run_batch recorded 'crash'.
Same command with TMPDIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/qahome: RESULT produced (win/soft path ran). Two later default-TMPDIR runs also worked.
expected: A run with no error and no RESULT is classed as a crash only after an error; the first run should produce a RESULT.
actual: One run returned no RESULT with no error line. Not reproduced in 2 further runs with default TMPDIR. Cause UNKNOWN (first run after editing bot_run.gd; possibly a script reimport).

steps: Run any market focus with a built workshop, e.g. Godot --headless --path . -s res://qa/bots/bot_run.gd -- --strategy=decent --seed=1 --market=bio --skip-tutorial. RESULT issues: warning_streak at cycle 28 'route 10 shows Waiting for room for 3+ cycles in a row'.
Count: 65 of 116 batch runs carry this warning.
expected: A route shows 'Waiting for room' only while storage is genuinely full, and clears when there is room.
actual: The warning persists for 3+ cycles in 65 runs. It looks like planet storage at its cap (BIO_3 relieves it in the bio focus). Whether the persistent wait is intended is UNKNOWN.
